name: Amasi scones
summary: Tall, tender scones made with tangy amasi instead of buttermilk, baked hot and fast, and split for butter, jam and grated cheese.
about: Many South African home bakers make scones with amasi, the thick fermented milk most households keep in the fridge. Its acidity reacts with the baking powder for a good rise and a soft crumb. They are a weekend breakfast, a tea-time treat and a lunch-box filler, eaten with butter, apricot jam and cheese or with cream.

ingredients.name: Amasi
ingredients.note: plus a little extra if needed

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.

Sift the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt into a large bowl. Add the butter and rub it in with your fingertips for 3–4 minutes, until the mixture looks like fine breadcrumbs with no large lumps of butter.
Beat the egg and amasi together in a jug, then set aside 1 tablespoon of the mixture for glazing.

Make a well in the flour, pour in the rest of the amasi mixture and cut it through with a table knife until it just comes together into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Add a spoonful more amasi if dry crumbs remain. Do not knead; overworking makes tough scones.

Turn onto a floured surface and pat gently into a round about 3 cm thick. Cut out scones with a floured 6 cm cutter, pressing straight down without twisting, and set them close together on the tray. Gather the scraps lightly and cut again, to make about 12.
Brush the tops with the reserved glaze and bake for 12–15 minutes, until well risen and golden and they sound hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool on a rack for 5 minutes, wrapped in a clean tea towel to keep the crust soft. Serve warm, split, with butter, jam and grated cheese.
prepNote: Best on the day; freeze extras and warm them for 5 minutes in a 180 °C oven.
